title: Public CORS RINEX to SPP vs RTK with RTKLIB demo5 and gnss_lib_py
summary: Downloads one day of public NOAA NGS CORS RINEX for a rover/base pair 30 km apart, runs RTKLIB demo5 rnx2rtkp in single-point and kinematic RTK modes with exact CLI flags, and scores both against the stations' published ITRF2020 coordinates (propagated for plate motion) in ENU. An optional gnss_lib_py weighted-least-squares SPP covers the same data in Python, after converting RINEX 2.11 to 3.
verified: ran on 2026-11-06 on real NOAA NGS CORS data (P730 rover, P731 base, 2024-04-09 12:00-14:00 GPST, GPS only, 241 epochs): RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 built in Docker (docker/Dockerfile) gave SPP E/N/U rms 0.62/1.24/1.02 m and RTK 0.084/0.055/0.071 m with 97% fix, scored by compare_pos.py against the propagated ITRF2020 sheet; gnss_lib_py 1.1.0 WLS (glp_spp.py, after fixing a GPST-vs-UTC epoch tag, per-chunk ephemeris selection and transmit-time SV states) gave 0.65/1.28/1.10 m. compare_pos.py's 4 unit tests ran with python3.14.7. Not verified: other days/stations, multi-GNSS, PPP, antenna phase-centre models, a native (non-Docker) RTKLIB build.
